exampleAnswers.title: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} -1 & -2 & 5 & \color{red}-3 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & \color{red}2 \\ 5 & 3 & 4 & \color{red}-2 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}\\ \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above $a_{44}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries above $a_{44}=1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} -1 & -2 & 5 & \color{black}-3 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & \color{black}2 \\ 5 & 3 & 4 & \color{black}-2 \\ \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}\\ \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} R_1:=R_1+3R_4 \\ R_2:=R_2+(-2)R_4 \\ R_3:=R_3+2R_4 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 5 & -2 & 14 & \color{red}0 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 & \color{red}0 \\ 9 & 3 & 10 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}\\ \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $4$th column, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 5 & -2 & 14 & \color{red}0 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 & \color{red}0 \\ 9 & 3 & 10 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}\\ \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}} \cdot (-1)^{4+4} \begin{vmatrix} 5 & -2 & 14 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 \\ 9 & 3 & 10 \\ \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 5 & -2 & 14 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 \\ 9 & 3 & 10 \\ \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

example.title: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} 4 & \color{red}-3 & 2& 5\\ -2 & \color{red}-1 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & \color{red}3 & -7& 6 \\ 3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & 3 & -5 \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above $a_{42}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries above $a_{42}=1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 4 & -3 & 2& 5\\ -2 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & 3 & -7 & 6 \\ \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}-5 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} R_1:=R_1+3R_4 \\ R_2:=R_2+R_4 \\ R_3:=R_3+(-3)R_4 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 13 & \color{red}0 & 11& -10\\ 1& \color{red}0 & 7 & -2 \\ -4& \color{red}0 & -16 & 21 \\ \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}-5 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 13 & \color{red}0 & 11& -10\\ 1 & \color{red}0 & 7 & -2 \\ -4 & \color{red}0 & -16 & 21 \\ \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}-5 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}} \cdot (-1)^{4+2} \begin{vmatrix} 13 & 11& -10\\ 1 & 7& -2 \\ -4 & -16 & 21 \\ \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 13 & 11& -10\\ 1 & 7& -2 \\ -4 & -16 & 21 \\ \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

example.title: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} 2& \color{red}-6 & -11 & -5 \\ -3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & 5 & 4 \\ 2 & \color{red}4 & -1 & 5 \\ -3 & \color{red}-2 & 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below $a_{22}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries above and below $a_{22}=2$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 2 & -6 & -11 & -5 \\ \color{blue}-3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{blue}5 & \color{blue}4 \\ 2 & 4 & -1 & 5 \\ -3 & -2 & 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} R_1:=R_1+3R_2 \\ R_3:=R_3+(-2)R_2 \\ R_4:=R_4+R_2 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} -7& \color{red}0 & 4 & 7 \\ \color{blue}-3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{blue}5 & \color{blue}4 \\ 8& \color{red}0 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & \color{red}0 & 6 & 2 \end{vmatrix} . \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} -7 & \color{red}0 & 4 & 7 \\ \color{blue}-3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{blue}5 & \color{blue}4 \\ 8 & \color{red}0 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & \color{red}0 & 6 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2}} \cdot (-1)^{2+2} \begin{vmatrix} -7 & 4 & 7 \\ 8 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & 6 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= 2 \begin{vmatrix} -7 & 4 & 7 \\ 8 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & 6 & 2 \end{vmatrix} . \end{align*}

example.title: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 3 & \color{red}1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & \color{red}-2 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-1} & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & \color{red}3 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below $a_{33}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries above and below $a_{33}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 & 5 \\ \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-1} & \color{blue}2 \\ -1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} R_1:=R_1+R_3 \\ R_2:=R_2+(-2)R_3 \\ R_4:=R_4+3R_3 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 6 & \color{red}0 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & \color{red}0 & 1 \\ \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-1} & \color{blue}2 \\ 2 & 7 & \color{red}0 & 8 \end{vmatrix} \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $3$rd column, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 6 & \color{red}0 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & \color{red}0 & 1 \\ \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-1} & \color{blue}2 \\ 2 & 7 & \color{red}0 & 8 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= ({\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-1}}) \cdot (-1)^{3+3} \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 6 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & 1 \\ 2 & 7 & 8 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= - \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 6 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & 1 \\ 2 & 7 & 8 \end{vmatrix} . \end{align*}

example.title: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} 3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-1} & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & \color{red}3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & \color{red}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & \color{red}2 & -1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below $a_{12}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries below $a_{12}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-1} & \color{blue}4 & \color{blue}3 \\ 2 & \color{black}3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & \color{black}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & \color{black}2 & -1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} R_2:=R_2+3R_1 \\ R_3:=R_3+(-1)R_1 \\ R_4:=R_4+2R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-1} & \color{blue}4 & \color{blue}3 \\ 11 & \color{red}0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & \color{red}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & \color{red}0 & 7 & 7 \end{vmatrix} . \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-1} & \color{blue}4 & \color{blue}3 \\ 11 & \color{red}0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & \color{red}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & \color{red}0 & 7 & 7 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= ({\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-1}}) \cdot (-1)^{1+2} \begin{vmatrix} 11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7 \end{vmatrix} . \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} -1 & 2 & -3 & -1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ \color{red}4 & \color{red}-2 & \color{red}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of $a_{44}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries to the left of $a_{44}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} -1 & 2 & -3 & \color{blue}-1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & \color{blue}2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & \color{blue}-2 \\ \color{black}4 & \color{black}-2 & \color{black}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_1:=C_1+(-4)C_4 \\ C_2:=C_2+2C_4 \\ C_3:=C_3+(-3)C_4 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 & \color{blue}-1 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 & \color{blue}2 \\ 11 & -3 & 10 & \color{blue}-2 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 & \color{blue}-1 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 & \color{blue}2 \\ 11 & -3 & 10 & \color{blue}-2 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}} \cdot (-1)^{4+4} \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 \\ 11 & -3 & 10 \\ \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 \\ 11 & -3 & 10 \\ \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

example.title: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} -2 & -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ \color{red}6 & \color{red}-4 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{red}2 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 & -3 \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of $a_{33}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of $a_{33}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} -2 & -4 & \color{blue}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & \color{blue}1 & 2 \\ \color{black}6 & \color{black}-4 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{black}2 \\ 2 & -3 & \color{blue}-2 & -3 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_1:=C_1+(-3)C_3 \\ C_2:=C_2+2C_3 \\ C_4:=C_4+(-1)C_3 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} -8 & 0 & \color{blue}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & \color{blue}1 & 1 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{red}0 \\ 8 & -7 & \color{blue}-2 & -1 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} -8 & 0 & \color{blue}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & \color{blue}1 & 1 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{red}0 \\ 8 & -7 & \color{blue}-2 & -1 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2}} \cdot (-1)^{3+3} \begin{vmatrix} -8 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -1 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= 2 \begin{vmatrix} -8 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -1 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 6 & 12 & -5 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{red}4 & \color{red}6 & \color{red}-4 \\ -3 & 1 & -8 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & 5 & -6 \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of $a_{21}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries to the right of $a_{21}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}4 & 6 & 12 & -5 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{black}4 & \color{black}6 & \color{black}-4 \\ \color{blue}-3 & 1 & -8 & 2 \\ \color{blue}5 & 2 & 5 & -6 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_2:=C_2+(-2)C_1 \\ C_3:=C_3+(-3)C_1 \\ C_4:=C_4+2C_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}4& -2 & 0 & 3 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}-3 & 7 & 1 & -4 \\ \color{blue}5 & -8 & -10 & 4 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}4& -2 & 0 & 3 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}-3 & 7 & 1 & -4 \\ \color{blue}5 & -8 & -10 & 4 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2}} \cdot (-1)^{2+1} \begin{vmatrix} -2 & 0& 3\\ 7 & 1 & -4 \\ -8 & -10 & 4 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= -2 \begin{vmatrix} -2 & 0& 3\\ 7 & 1 & -4 \\ -8 & -10 & 4 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & 7 & -5 \\ -2 & 9 & -2 & 7 \\ 5 & 3 & 6 & 6\\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}-2 & \color{red}3 & \color{red}-1 \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of $a_{41}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries to the right of $a_{41}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}3 & 1 & 7 & -5 \\ \color{blue}-2 & 9 & -2 & 7 \\ \color{blue}5 & 3 & 6 & 6\\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{black}-2 & \color{black}3 & \color{black}-1 \\ \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_2:=C_2+2C_1 \\ C_3:=C_3+(-3)C_1 \\ C_4:=C_4+C_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}3& 7 & -2 & -2 \\ \color{blue}-2 & 5 & 4 & 5 \\ \color{blue}5 & 13 & -9 & 11\\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}3& 7 & -2 & -2 \\ \color{blue}-2 & 5 & 4 & 5 \\ \color{blue}5 & 13 & -9 & 11\\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}} \cdot (-1)^{4+1} \begin{vmatrix} 7 & -2& -2\\ 5 & 4 & 5 \\ 13 & -9 & 11 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= - \begin{vmatrix} 7 & -2& -2\\ 5 & 4 & 5 \\ 13 & -9 & 11 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} \color{red}1 & \color{red}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}-4 \\ -4 & 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & -2 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of $a_{13}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of $a_{13}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{black}1 & \color{black}3 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{black}-4 \\ -4 & 2 & \color{blue}2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2 & \color{blue}-1 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & \color{blue}-2 & 2 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_1:=C_1+(-1)C_3 \\ C_2:=C_2+(-3)C_3 \\ C_4:=C_4+4C_3 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}0 \\ -6 & -4 & \color{blue}2 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & \color{blue}-1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & \color{blue}-2 & -6 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $1$st row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}0 \\ -6 & -4 & \color{blue}2 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & \color{blue}-1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & \color{blue}-2 & -6 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}} \cdot (-1)^{1+3} \begin{vmatrix} -6 & -4 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & -6 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} -6 & -4 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & -6 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

example.title: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations

exampleAnswers.title: Computing 4x4 Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

question.text:
Calculate the value of $ \, \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 9 & -6 & -3 \\ -5 & -6 & 10 & 12 \\ 2 & 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 4 & 8 & -8 & -2 \end{vmatrix}. $

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of $a_{11}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4 \times 4$ determinant to a $3 \times 3$ determinant.
question.explanation:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of $a_{11}=3$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{3} & 9 & -6 & -3 \\ \color{blue}-5 & -6 & 10 & 12 \\ \color{blue}2 & 2 & -1 & -1 \\ \color{blue}4 & 8 & -8 & -2 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_2:=C_2+(-3)C_1 \\ C_3:=C_3+2C_1 \\ C_4:=C_4+C_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{3} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}-5 & 9 & 0 & 7 \\ \color{blue}2 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ \color{blue}4 & -4 & 0 & 2 \end{vmatrix} . \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $1$st row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{3} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}-5 & 9 & 0 & 7 \\ \color{blue}2 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ \color{blue}4 & -4 & 0 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{3}} \cdot (-1)^{1+1} \begin{vmatrix} 9 & 0 & 7 \\ -4 & 3 & 1 \\ -4 & 0 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= 3\cdot \begin{vmatrix} 9 & \color{red}0 & 7 \\ -4 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{3} & 1 \\ -4 & \color{red}0 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= 3\cdot ({\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{3}}) \cdot (-1)^{2+2} \begin{vmatrix} 9 & 7 \\ -4 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\\[5pt] &= 9(18+28) \\[5pt] &= 9(46) \\[5pt] &= 414. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing 4x4 Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

question.text:
Calculate the value of $ \, \begin{vmatrix} -1 & 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & -4 & -1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 4 & -3 & 1 & -4 \end{vmatrix}. $

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below $a_{14}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4 \times 4$ determinant to a $3 \times 3$ determinant.
question.explanation:
Using elementary row operations, let's make entries below $a_{14}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}-1 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}-2 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} \\ 3 & -4 & -1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 4 & -3 & 1 & -4 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} R_2:=R_2+(-3)R_1 \\ R_3:=R_3+(-2)R_1 \\ R_4:=R_4+4R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}-1 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}-2 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} \\ 6 & -13 & 5 & \color{red}0 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 & \color{red}0 \\ 0 & 9 & -7 & \color{red}0 \\ \end{vmatrix} . \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $4$th column, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}-1 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}-2 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} \\ 6 & -13 & 5 & \color{red}0 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 & \color{red}0 \\ 0 & 9 & -7 & \color{red}0 \\ \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}} \cdot (-1)^{1+4} \begin{vmatrix} 6 & -13 & 5\\ 0 & -5 & -1\\ 0 & 9 & -7 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= - \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{6} & -13 & 5\\ \color{red}0 & -5 & -1\\ \color{red}0 & 9 & -7 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= (-1)\cdot {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{6}} \cdot (-1)^{1+1} \begin{vmatrix} -5 & -1\\ 9 & -7 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= -6(35-(-9)) \\[5pt] &= -264. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing 4x4 Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

question.text:
Calculate the value of $ \, \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}. $

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below $a_{11}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4 \times 4$ determinant to a $3 \times 3$ determinant.
question.explanation:
Using elementary row operations, let's make entries below $a_{11}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}-1 & \color{blue}1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} R_2:=R_2+(-1)R_1 \\ R_3:=R_3+(-1)R_1 \\ R_4:=R_4+R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{blue}1 &\color{blue} -1 & \color{blue}1 \\ \color{red}0 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ \color{red}0 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ \color{red}0 & 0 & -2 & 2 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $1$st column, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{blue}1 &\color{blue} -1 & \color{blue}1 \\ \color{red}0 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ \color{red}0 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ \color{red}0 & 0 & -2 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}} \cdot (-1)^{1+1} \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{red}0 & 2 & 1 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & -1 & 2 \\ \color{red}0 & -2 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}} \cdot (-1)^{2+1} \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= -(4-(-2)) \\[5pt] &= -6. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing 4x4 Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

question.text:
Calculate the value of $ \, \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 4 & 4 & -4 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & -2 \end{vmatrix}. $

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of $a_{21}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4 \times 4$ determinant to a $3 \times 3$ determinant.
question.explanation:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of $a_{21}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ \color{blue}2 & 4 & 4 & -4 \\ \color{blue}-2 & 1 & -2 & -2 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_2:=C_2+(-2)C_1 \\ C_3:=C_3+(-3)C_1 \\ C_4:=C_4+2C_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ \color{blue}-2 & 5 & 4 & -6 \end{vmatrix} . \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ \color{blue}-2 & 5 & 4 & -6 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}} \cdot (-1)^{2+1} \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 4 & -6 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= - \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -2 & 1 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-2} & \color{red}0 \\ 5 & 4 & -6 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= (-1) \cdot ({\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-2}}) \cdot (-1)^{2+2} \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 5 & -6 \end{vmatrix}\\[5pt] &= 2(-6-5) \\[5pt] &= -22. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing 4x4 Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

question.text:
Calculate the value of $ \, \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 6 & -4 \\ -3 & 3 & -9 & 5 \end{vmatrix}. $

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of $a_{11}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4 \times 4$ determinant to a $3 \times 3$ determinant.
question.explanation:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of $a_{11}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ \color{blue}2 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ \color{blue}3 & -2 & 6 & -4 \\ \color{blue}-3 & 3 & -9 & 5 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_2:=C_2+(-2)C_1 \\ C_3:=C_3+(-3)C_1 \\ C_4:=C_4+2C_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}2 & -3 & 0 & 5 \\ \color{blue}3 & -8 & -3 & 2 \\ \color{blue}-3 & 9 & 0 & -1 \end{vmatrix} . \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $1$st row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}2 & -3 & 0 & 5 \\ \color{blue}3 & -8 & -3 & 2 \\ \color{blue}-3 & 9 & 0 & -1 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}} \cdot (-1)^{1+1} \begin{vmatrix} -3 & 0 & 5 \\ -8 & -3 & 2 \\ 9 & 0 & -1 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} -3 & \color{red}0 & 5 \\ -8 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-3} & 2 \\ 9 & \color{red}0 & -1 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= ({\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-3}}) \cdot (-1)^{2+2} \begin{vmatrix} -3 & 5 \\ 9 & -1 \end{vmatrix}\\[5pt] &= -3(3-45) \\[5pt] &= 126. \end{align*}
